blurb: Alice follows a White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole into a world where nothing makes sense.
source: Text: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll (1865), from the Standard Ebooks edition. Public domain.

streets.name: Down the Rabbit-Hole
streets.blurb: The rabbit-hole dips suddenly down, and Alice falls past cupboards and book-shelves.
streets.how: Drift gently down the hole from shelf to shelf. Grab at least three jars of marmalade on the way to the bottom.

params.objective: Fall all the way to the bottom
params.done: Thump! Down on a heap of sticks and dry leaves, and the fall is over.

streets.name: The Pool of Tears
streets.blurb: Alice cried so much when she was nine feet high that the hall is now a pool of tears.
streets.how: Hop across the floating things to the far shore, picking up the key, the bottle and the little cake on the way. Falling in only sends you back to the shore.

params.label: found
params.done: Out of the pool and dripping wet. Now to get dry…

streets.name: The Caucus-Race
streets.blurb: The best thing to get dry, says the Dodo, is a Caucus-race.
streets.how: Run round the course with everyone else. Two laps and the race is over — and everybody wins.

params.objective: Run two laps of the Caucus-race
params.done: Everybody has won, and all must have prizes!

streets.name: The Rabbit's House
streets.blurb: Alice drank from a little bottle in the White Rabbit’s house — and now she fills the whole room.
streets.how: Look round the room for clues, then work out how to get out.

params.objective: Work out how to get out of the house

clues.label: The little bottle
clues.text: A little bottle stood near the looking-glass. There was no label this time — and Alice drank from it anyway. Now she can’t get out at the door.

clues.label: The window
clues.text: Someone outside shouts “a barrowful will do, to begin with!” — and a shower of little pebbles comes rattling in.

clues.label: The pebbles
clues.text: The pebbles on the floor are all turning into little cakes.

solve.label: The door
solve.prompt: How can Alice get small enough to get out?
options: Eat one of the little cakes
Drink the rest of the bottle
Wait for Bill the Lizard to pull her out
solve.hint: Things to eat and drink keep changing Alice’s size. Which one is new?

params.done: Alice shrinks, runs out of the house and off into a thick wood.

streets.name: The Caterpillar
streets.blurb: A large blue caterpillar sits on top of a mushroom, quietly smoking a long hookah and taking no notice of anybody.
streets.how: Climb the giant mushroom from cap to cap to reach the Caterpillar at the top.

finale.say: Who are YOU? … One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.

params.done: Alice nibbles a bit of each side, and gets herself back to her right size.

streets.name: Pig and Pepper
streets.blurb: The Duchess’s kitchen is full of smoke and pepper, and the cook is throwing everything within reach.
streets.how: Dodge the pepper, the frying-pans and the plates for 30 seconds.

params.objective: Dodge the pepper and the pans!
params.done: Out of the kitchen — and the baby turns out to be a pig.

streets.name: The Mad Tea-Party
streets.blurb: A table set out under a tree, with the March Hare, the Hatter and a sleepy Dormouse squeezed at one corner.
streets.how: Look at the clock, the cups and the guests, then work out the seat-moving pattern.

params.objective: Work out why they keep moving round the table

clues.label: The Hatter’s watch
clues.text: The watch tells the day of the month, but doesn’t tell what o’clock it is. The Hatter says that ever since he quarrelled with Time, it’s always six o’clock.

clues.label: The tea things
clues.text: A very long table, laid for lots of people — with dirty cups all along one side.

clues.label: The Dormouse
clues.text: The Dormouse is fast asleep, being used as a cushion by the other two.

solve.label: The empty seats
solve.prompt: It’s always tea-time, and there’s no time to wash up. So what do they do?
options: Move one place on round the table, to a clean cup
Wash the cups in the teapot
solve.hint: Listen to what the Hatter says when he wants a clean cup.

params.done: “Let’s all move one place on!” And round they go.

streets.name: The Croquet-Ground
streets.blurb: The balls are live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes, and the soldiers stand on their hands to make the arches.
streets.how: Drag back from the hedgehog to hit it through the soldier-hoop, then into the flag. The hoop keeps walking off!

params.objective: Through the soldier, then to the flag
params.done: You played the Queen’s croquet — and kept your head!

streets.name: The Mock Turtle's Story
streets.blurb: The Mock Turtle remembers his school days in the sea, and all the odd things he learned there.
streets.how: Find all six of the Mock Turtle’s school subjects scattered along the shore.

params.label: subjects
params.objective: Find the Mock Turtle’s six subjects

finale.say: That’s the reason they’re called lessons — because they lessen from day to day!

params.done: Ten hours the first day, nine the next, and so on…

streets.name: The Lobster Quadrille
streets.blurb: The Gryphon and the Mock Turtle show Alice the Lobster Quadrille.
streets.how: Keep to the beat: hit each lobster, turtle and whiting as it reaches the line.

params.done: Will you, won’t you, will you, won’t you, will you join the dance?

streets.name: Who Stole the Tarts?
streets.blurb: The Knave of Hearts is on trial for stealing the Queen’s tarts.
streets.how: Search the courtroom for the six things the court will want to see.

params.label: pieces of evidence
params.objective: Gather the evidence around the court
params.done: “Call the next witness!” said the King.

skyRun.name: The Cheshire Cat's Treetops
skyRun.blurb: a treetop course where the branches fade in and out, just like the Cat.
skyRun.how: Climb the tree to the top. Blue branches vanish and come back — wait for them!

params.objective: Climb to the Cheshire Cat’s branch
params.done: All that’s left is the grin…

sideQuest.title: The White Rabbit's Gloves and Fan

steps.text: Talk to the White Rabbit outside Wonderland.
steps.say: Oh my dear paws! Oh my fur and whiskers! I’ve dropped my white kid gloves and my fan somewhere in the garden, and the Duchess will be savage!

steps.text: Find the White Rabbit’s gloves and fan around Wonderland.
Give the gloves and fan back to the White Rabbit.
steps.say: My gloves! My fan! Now I shan’t be late — well, not very late. Thank you!

vault.name: The Trial of the Knave
vault.blurb: an escape room in the Queen's courtroom, about the whole of Wonderland.
vault.intro: The court is in session, and the Queen wants the sentence first. Four locks hold the courtroom door. Show you know what really happened in Wonderland — and whether the evidence is real.

stations.label: The White Rabbit’s scroll
stations.text: The White Rabbit has mixed up the order of Alice’s adventures. Put them right.
stations.lesson: Down the rabbit-hole, through the pool of tears, and all the way to the trial.

items: Swimming in the pool of tears
The trial of the Knave of Hearts
solve.hint: The rabbit-hole is first and the trial is last.

stations.label: The jury-box
stations.text: The jurors have written names on their slates. Match each character to what they did.
stations.lesson: Wonderland is full of characters who all think they make perfect sense.

solve.hint: Think about where Alice met each of them.

stations.label: The “evidence”
stations.text: The White Rabbit has just picked up a paper: a set of verses. It isn’t in the Knave’s handwriting, and there’s no name signed at the end.
stations.lesson: Proper evidence has to show something. These verses prove nothing at all.

solve.prompt: Does this paper prove the Knave stole the tarts?
options: No — it isn’t his writing, it isn’t signed, and it doesn’t even make sense
Yes — not signing it proves he’s guilty
Yes — because the Queen says so
solve.hint: Alice says she doesn’t believe there’s an atom of meaning in it.

quiz.label: The King’s notebook
quiz.lesson: You remembered all of Wonderland — and it was only a pack of cards.

vault.openText: “You’re nothing but a pack of cards!” The whole pack rises up into the air — and the door flies open.
vault.outro: Alice grows to her full size, the cards come flying down, and she wakes on the bank with her head in her sister’s lap.
